Below is a consolidated post‐mortem of what went wrong in each group, the minimal YAML changes to fix it, how to verify the fixes, and how you could have caught all of this in CI before ever hitting prod.

---

## 1. Diagnose Each Error Type

| Group                   | Error                                                                                              | Root cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Azure OpenAI**        | `{"code":"DeploymentNotFound","message":"The API deployment for this resource does not exist…"}`     | You never told LiteLLM to use your _Azure_ deployment IDs (and correct API version). By using `model: azure/gpt‑4` (etc.) without `api_type: azure`/real deployment names, Azure looked for a deployment literally called “azure/gpt‑4.” |
| **Anthropic Claude**    | `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"model: field required"}}`      | The model string you supplied (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514` etc.) is not a valid Anthropic model tag in LiteLLM’s registry, so LiteLLM never injected a `"model": …` into the JSON. Anthropic therefore complains “model: field required.” |
| **Groq Llama‑3**        | `{"message":"max_tokens exceeds the model context window. Requested: 32768, Context window: 8192"}` | You configured `max_tokens: 32768` for both Groq models—but their published context window is **8 192**, so Groq’s API outright rejects any ask larger than the model’s window.                                                    |

---

## 2. Minimal Config Fixes

Below are only the changed lines (so you can drop them into your existing `litellm_config.yaml`).  

```diff
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Group B: Azure OpenAI models
-  - model_name: azure-gpt4
-    litellm_params:
-      model: azure/gpt-4
-      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
-      api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com
-      api_version: "2024-02-15-preview"
+  - model_name: azure-gpt4
+    litellm_params:
+      api_type: azure                       # ← tell the OpenAI client this is Azure
+      model: gpt-4-deployment               # ← your actual Azure deployment name in the portal
+      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
+      api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com
+      api_version: "2023-05-15"             # ← GA‐supported version for your deployment

-  - model_name: azure-gpt4-mini
-    litellm_params:
-      model: azure/gpt-4o-mini
-      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
-      api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com
-      api_version: "2024-02-15-preview"
+  - model_name: azure-gpt4-mini
+    litellm_params:
+      api_type: azure
+      model: gpt-4o-mini-deployment         # ← your actual Azure deployment name
+      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
+      api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com
+      api_version: "2023-05-15"

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Group C: Anthropic models
-  - model_name: claude-opus
-    litellm_params:
-      model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514
-      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
-      max_tokens: 4096
+  - model_name: claude-opus
+    litellm_params:
+      model: anthropic/claude-opus-4         # ← valid model ID (no bogus date suffix!)
+      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
+      api_base: https://api.anthropic.com/v1  # ← point at Anthropic’s endpoint
+      max_tokens: 4096

-  - model_name: claude-sonnet
-    litellm_params:
-      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514
-      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
-      max_tokens: 4096
+  - model_name: claude-sonnet
+    litellm_params:
+      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4       # ← valid model ID
+      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
+      api_base: https://api.anthropic.com/v1
+      max_tokens: 4096

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Group E: Groq models
-  - model_name: llama-fast
-    litellm_params:
-      model: groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile
-      api_key: os.environ/GROQ_API_KEY
-      max_tokens: 32768
+  - model_name: llama-fast
+    litellm_params:
+      # … model & api_key unchanged …
+      max_tokens: 8192                       # ← must not exceed the 8 192 token window

-  - model_name: llama-mini
-    litellm_params:
-      model: groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant
-      api_key: os.environ/GROQ_API_KEY
-      max_tokens: 32768
+  - model_name: llama-mini
+    litellm_params:
+      # … model & api_key unchanged …
+      max_tokens: 8192
```

---

## 3. Validation Checklist

After you drop in those fixes, run these steps **before** you promote to production:

| Step                              | Command / Action                                                   | What you verify                                      |
|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| 1. Config‐schema linting & parse  | `lite llm validate-config --file litellm_config.yaml`              | YAML is syntactically valid & schema‐compliant       |
| 2. Health‐check all providers     | `lite llm healthcheck`                                             | Connectivity & credentials for every model           |
| 3. Smoke‐test each service        | ```bash
lite llm run azure-gpt4   --prompt "hello" --max-tokens 5
lite llm run claude-opus  --prompt "hello" --max-tokens 5
lite llm run llama-fast   --prompt "hello" --max-tokens 5
``` | No 4xx/5xx errors; you get back a valid “choices” / completion |
| 4. Inspect logs                   | Tail your LiteLLM logs for any lingering 404/400 errors            | All errors cleared                                   |

---

## 4. Preventing It in CI

To catch **all three** of these classes of mistakes before they ever go live, add CI/validation gates:

| Mistake class               | Guard / CI‑Check                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Azure deployment mis‑match  | Schema rule: if `api_base` contains `.openai.azure.com`, require `api_type: azure` and that `model` ∈ allowed Azure deployment list. |
| Anthropic invalid model     | Schema rule: validated `model` field against Anthropic’s published model‐ID allowlist (e.g. `claude-opus-4`, `claude-sonnet-4`). |
| Context‐window exceedance   | Static check: assert `max_tokens ≤ { model:context_window }` using a small lookup table (e.g. Groq ⇒ 8192).    |
| General config linting      | `lite llm validate-config` in pre‑commit or CI pipeline                                                          |
| Quick API smoke tests       | Run a minimal “hello world” prompt on every configured model (can be mocked or real)                          |

By combining **schema linting** (YAML‐based rules), **static parameter checks** (max_tokens, allow‑lists), and **runtime smoke tests**, you will catch invalid deployments, missing fields, bad model IDs or token‐window overshoots in your CI/CD pipeline — long before any user ever sees a 404 or 400 in production.
